summary: This paper presents a fault-tolerant quantum error correction framework based on singlet-triplet (dual-spin) qubits in semiconductor devices, establishing them as natural erasure qubits. A hardware-efficient leakage-detection protocol projects leaked qubits back to the computational subspace without measurement feedback, and when combined with the XZZX surface code achieves a twofold threshold increase and orders-of-magnitude logical error rate reductions.
motivation: Singlet-triplet qubits are intrinsically protected against phase noise and support high-fidelity shuttling (demonstrated at 99.99% per increment), making them attractive for scalable shuttling-based architectures. However, their leakage out of the odd-parity computational subspace must be detected and corrected without introducing excessive overhead.
method: The work designs stabilizer circuits using exchange gates (H, CZ) and driven gates (CNOT) that convert Pauli errors into detectable leakage. An erasure-detection circuit unitarily transfers state to a fresh pair and measures the old pair, automatically projecting leakage back without feedback. Two implementations are analyzed: exchange-only circuits yielding balanced $X/Z$/erasure noise, and CNOT-based circuits achieving bias-preserving $Z$-dominant noise for use with the XZZX surface code.
result: Simulations show the singlet-triplet CSS encoding achieves threshold $p_c = 0.49\%$ versus $0.45\%$ for Loss-DiVincenzo qubits, while the XZZX variant reaches $p_c = 1.3\%$. At equal electron count and $p_\mathrm{sh,LD} = 0.5\%$ shuttling error (10 μm shuttling), the ST+XZZX scheme delivers orders-of-magnitude lower logical error rates when $p_\mathrm{sh,ST} \leq p_\mathrm{sh,LD}$, with effective distances benefiting from the reduced resource overhead per dual-spin qubit.
